description:
Hey! I’m Sharon (Mechatronics Engineering student from Mexico), joining forces with my friend Carlo (our tech & computer systems guy). Together we bring strong engineering, programming, and problem-solving skills to tackle this challenge.

We’re looking to build an intuitive tool that spots real, significant trends in Earth science data—and have a great time doing it.

We’d love to add teammates skilled in.
summary: EcoDelta developed trendkit, an open-source Python scientific toolkit designed to detect, quantify, and validate real environmental trends from NASA Earth observation data without falling into common statistical traps. Raw climate time series often hide true trends behind strong seasonal cycles or trigger false alarms due to autocorrelation and multiple-grid testing. Trendkit automates the entire analytical pipeline: it computes area-weighted regional averages, removes seasonal climatology, calculates robust decadal rates of change using Sen’s slope with 95% confidence intervals, and tests statistical significance using an autocorrelation-corrected Mann-Kendall test (Yue-Wang AR1) alongside an OLS t-test cross-check. For spatial maps, it applies Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) control to eliminate false positives across thousands of grid cells, delivering clear verdicts and plain-language scientific warnings.
details:
• What It Does & How It Works EcoDelta’s trendkit turns raw satellite and climate model time series into statistically defensible trend reports. Given a regional time series or spatial grid (such as monthly 2-meter air temperature from NASA POWER), the pipeline executes six automated steps:
    Tools, Data & Validation Built in Python using numpy and validated against scipy, statsmodels, and pymannkendall(matching reference implementations to 10−810−8–10−1210−12 precision). Tested with real monthly temperature (T2M) data from NASA POWER and benchmarked on 90×18090×180 global grids in ~52 seconds.
    1. Time & Spatial Aggregation: Converts dates into decimal years and computes cosine-latitude area-weighted regional means so polar and tropical grid cells are properly balanced.
    2. Deseasonalization: Strips out recurring annual cycles (summer/winter swings) by computing monthly climatologies and anomalies, reducing standard error by up to ~25x so subtle long-term trends become visible.
    3. Robust Rate of Change: Estimates the rate of change per decade using Sen’s slope (median of all pairwise slopes, making it immune to outliers) along with autocorrelation-adjusted 95% confidence intervals.
    4. Autocorrelation-Corrected Significance Testing: Applies the Mann-Kendall test using the Yue-Wang AR(1) variance inflation correction (selected after Monte Carlo benchmarking of 2,000 simulations against Hamed-Rao and TFPW methods) to keep false-alarm rates near the ideal 5% threshold, cross-checked with AR(1)-adjusted Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression and Student's t-test.
    5. Spatial False Discovery Control: When analyzing full maps, applies the Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) procedure (q=0.05q=0.05) to prevent hundreds of grid cells from showing false trends purely by chance.
    6. Automated Quality Verdicts: Enforces minimum data standards (≥10≥10 years and ≥80%≥80%valid data) and outputs JSON-ready reports with clear verdicts ("increasing", "decreasing", "no significant trend", or "insufficient data") plus plain-language warnings.
